newsitem.title: USA: Boston FY 98 budget ups debt service to $90.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Boston FY 98 budget ups debt service to $90.6 mln.

text.p: Boston Mayor Thomas Menino's tentative $1.4 billion budget for the fiscal year beginning July 1 will hike city spending on personnel as well as debt service.

The fixed-cost portion of the city budget -- pensions, debt service and state charges for the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority -- is projected to increase about five percent to $254 milllion, the city's budget director said.

The largest increase is in the annual debt service which is to rise to $90.6 million from $83 million reflecting increased spending for school improvements, some of the new police headquarters and the first installment on $38 million in antcipated renovations for the libraries.
The mayor's budget also calls for increasing the city's work force by 375 jobs - mostly in the areas of education and public safety.
Standard & Poor's Corp rates Boston's general obligation bonds A-plus with a stable outlook, while Moody's Investors Service Inc rates them A1.
